title: Book Two · Chapter 49: The Slow Corner
story:
On Sunday, Dad checks the blue bike in the yard. Ronan holds the seat. Mum is putting on her walking shoes.

“The little square?” Ronan asks.

“Yes,” Dad says. “We can practise there.”

Ronan presses the brake. Dad moves the bike forward a little. It stops. Then Dad lets Ronan take the handlebars.

They walk the narrow street first. The old bell is on the blue handlebar. Ronan keeps his thumb away from it beside Mr Qiu's table.

“I can see you,” Mr Qiu says. “No bell needed in my doorway.”

At the square, Mum walks around the outside. Dad stays beside Ronan. The middle is clear, with only a few dry leaves near the wall.

Ronan starts slowly. He makes one wide turn and comes back. His feet stay on the pedals. At the next corner, he presses the brake.

Ronan puts one foot down.

Dad stops beside him.

“Again?”

“Yes.”

The next turn is easier. Ronan looks toward the open part of the square. He does not watch only his front wheel.

Mum walks past them.

“Two legs are still useful,” she says.

Ronan makes a small circle and comes up beside her.

“Two wheels are useful, too.”

“Mine can climb steps.”

“Mine can ring.”

He gives the bell one small press. Mum laughs and walks ahead.

A woman enters the square with a basket. A small child is beside her. They cross toward the opposite doorway.

Ronan stops. He waits with both feet on the ground. Dad stands between the bike and the child's path.

The child looks at the bell.

“Can it ring?”

“Yes,” Ronan says.

He keeps the bike still and rings it once. The child smiles. The woman thanks him and goes through the doorway.

Ronan wants another long turn, but two boys now come with a ball. There is less clear space.

“We can stop here,” Dad says.

Ronan looks at the ball, then at his bike.

“One small turn?”

“Not across their game.”

Ronan turns the bike by hand. He walks it to the side. Mum comes back from her walk and takes her water bottle out.

They sit on the low wall. Dad takes the empty place at the end. His knees are much higher than Ronan's.

“Your bike is too small for me,” he says. “I need room for these.”

Mum looks at his knees. “Walk with me, then. There is room for them here.”

Ronan laughs and drinks some water.

On the way home, a cart blocks part of their usual narrow lane. Mum points to the next turn. They take the wider road instead. Ronan pushes the bike beside Dad.

At home, he parks it clear of the gate. Mum takes off her walking shoes. There is dust on the ends, but her blue skirt stays clean.

Ronan goes to the kitchen for three cups. Dad brings the water. Mum takes the chair near the window and puts her feet up for a moment.

“Now my two legs need a rest,” she says.

Ronan sits beside her with his cup. The bike stays in the yard. They can see its blue wheel through the open door.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

brake＝刹车；corner＝转角；slowly＝慢慢地；bell＝铃。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan在公共场地怎样照顾别人的通行？
2. 一家人为什么改变了回家的路线？

## 读句子

**Ronan / puts / one foot down.** Ronan／把一只脚／放到地上。
